question.text: Ammonia forms the complex ion $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$ with copper ions in alkaline solutions but not in acidic solutions. What is the reason for it?

options.text: In acidic solutions protons coordinate with ammonia molecules forming $\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}$ ions and $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ molecules are not available.
In alkaline solutions insoluble $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ is precipitated which is soluble in excess of any alkali.
Copper hydroxide is an amphoteric substance.
In acidic solutions hydration protects copper ions.
